help.intro: A stock adjustment adds or removes units by hand, where no document moved the goods: something broke or went missing, a sample came back, or a shelf audit disagrees with the books.
help.step_1_body: Pick the warehouse, the variant, how many and why - damaged, expired, lost, theft, a sample given away, or an audit that found fewer. The units leave the oldest batches first, the same order a shipment takes them in, and the ledger records each batch at its cost.
help.step_2_body: Units come back - found, a sample returned, returned goods, or an audit that found more. They go into recent batches that have sold some; a batch never holds more than it arrived with, so goods with nowhere to go have to come in on a goods receipt.
help.step_3_body: A wrong entry is reversed, never edited: the units go back where they came from and the ledger records the reversal. Units that were added cannot be taken back once they were sold - post a new adjustment instead.
help.note: Reservations are not checked: a removal records what happened, so it can leave a variant promised beyond what it holds. The variant stock window shows that as negative available.
